 - Prepare and/or support federal, state/provincial, and local tax filings across all legal entities, coordinating with external tax advisors as needed.

 - Gain exposure to banking relationships, account structures, and treasury tools/platforms.

 - Assist with intercompany funding tracking and foreign currency exposure considerations.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We are looking for a hands-on Technical Lead Manager (Release Qual & Integration) to establish and lead Release Integration Testing within Release & Feature Qualification for AI Inference Core.

The Production Engine for Inference Core — turning integrated features into reliable production releases.

You will define the quality strategy across the pre-release and release cycle, from feature and model integration through branch stability, release qualification, deployment, and post-release learning. You will work across AI frameworks, runtime, compiler, kernels, distributed systems, infrastructure, and hardware to make release risk visible and actionable.

This is a technical-leadership role, not a coordination-only position. You will design test architecture, lead difficult debugging and release decisions, mentor engineers, and write software and automation alongside the team.

Release Integration Testing (RIT) is the bridge between feature qualification and release qualification. Feature teams retain ownership of feature design, feature-level qualification, and feature regression. Release Integration Testing owns inference-core integration strategy, inference-path readiness approval, integrated cross-stack validation, and first-pass rollout triage.

WHAT MAKES THIS ROLE DISTINCT

 - Dedicated Release Integration Testing ownership: Engage before feature qualification completes while keeping the boundary clear: feature teams own feature behavior and qualification; Release Integration Testing owns integration strategy, readiness approval, integrated validation, and first-pass rollout triage.

 - Inference-path readiness gate: Require evidence across unit, simulation, benchmark, feature, and integration testing, with explicit coverage gaps before release entry.

 - Cross-stack test strategy: Define risk-based E2E and regression coverage for features spanning components, organizations, software layers, infrastructure, and hardware.

 - Branch and rollout leadership: Establish measurable health standards for master and release branches, and coordinate inference-impacting rollout across multiple product and release projects.

 - Hands-on technical authority: Lead through code, test architecture, difficult debugging, quality metrics, and evidence-based release decisions.

 - Team multiplier: Raise the technical bar, mentor engineers, and align feature, infrastructure, integration, qualification, and release teams.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

 - Define the Release Integration Testing strategy, engagement criteria, ownership boundaries, entry and exit criteria, coverage expectations, and escalation thresholds for AI Inference Core.

 - Engage early on high-risk inference changes; identify dependencies and interaction risks across runtime, host, device programming, memory, scheduling, model execution, infrastructure, and hardware.

 - Own the inference-path readiness gate by reviewing unit, simulation, benchmark, feature-test, and integration evidence, documenting gaps, and approving integration readiness before release entry.

 - Lead integrated inference E2E validation across features and the cloud-to-wafer stack; promote durable feature tests and add risk-based scenarios to release regression.

 - Improve master and release-branch stability through actionable health metrics, failure classification, release-quality reporting, dashboards, qualification workflows, and release pipelines.

 - Lead first-pass regression and rollout triage, coordinate owners through resolution, drive RCA, place missing coverage at the correct layer, and plan rollout across multiple product and release projects.

 - Partner with and mentor SDETs, feature teams, Integration, Core Infra, release owners, and deployment teams; between active engagements, advance automation efficiency, diagnostics, probes, and roadmap test planning.

MINIMUM SKILLS & QUALIFICATIONS

 - Strong software-engineering fundamentals and programming ability in Python Go, or a similar language.

 - Demonstrated technical leadership in software quality, test infrastructure, systems validation, release engineering, or complex software integration.

 - Experience designing automation and test architecture for distributed, systems-level, infrastructure, or AI software.

 - Proven ability to break down ambiguous cross-stack failures, form hypotheses, gather evidence, and drive issues to resolution.

 - Strong understanding of risk-based testing, release readiness, regression strategy, failure analysis, and quality metrics.

 - Ability to influence and align multiple engineering teams without relying solely on organizational authority.

 - Clear communication and sound judgment during high-pressure release situations, including the ability to explain technical risk to engineering and leadership audiences.

PREFERRED SKILLS

 - Experience with software/hardware co-design, hardware accelerators, compilers, kernels, runtimes, or low-level systems.

 - Experience with AI infrastructure, model deployment, LLMs, multimodal workloads, or large-scale compute clusters.

 - Experience building test frameworks, distributed test systems, release pipelines, dashboards, or internal developer tooling.

 - Experience with performance testing, profiling, observability, fault injection, reliability, or production failure analysis.

 - Experience managing geographically distributed teams across multiple regions and time zones is preferred

 - Experience in a startup or similarly fast-moving, resource-constrained engineering environment.

 - Track record of taking a quality or release capability from zero to one and scaling it across teams.

 - Familiarity with containers, cluster orchestration, cloud infrastructure, CI/CD, or high-performance computing.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 - Release readiness is based on explicit criteria and high-signal evidence rather than intuition.

 - Fewer inference-path integration defects are first discovered in final release qualification or production.

 - Cross-component risks are found earlier, debug cycles are shorter, and coverage ownership is explicit.

 - Master and release-branch health is measurable, actionable, and steadily improving.

 - Test automation and release infrastructure shorten feedback loops without sacrificing signal quality.

 - Release metrics and reports drive clear decisions, ownership, and predictable feature rollout.

 - Engineers across the organization are more effective because Release Integration Testing provides strong technical direction, tooling, and mentorship.

LOCATION

À propos du poste

À titre de gestionnaire de l'ingénierie pour l'équipe du grand livre auxiliaire, vous serez responsable du système de référence pour chaque transaction financière chez Hopper, assurant l'exactitude des rapports et le rapprochement de tous les mouvements de fonds dans notre écosystème.

 Chaque équipe qui traite des transactions, tant pour la réservation que pour l'après-réservation, dépend du grand livre auxiliaire; vous façonnerez donc l'architecture de la plateforme financière d'Hopper aux côtés des équipes Finances, Comptabilité, Paiements et des équipes d'ingénierie produit qui s'y appuient. Vous serez la personne responsable principale sur le plan technique d'un système où l'exactitude et la traçabilité complète comptent plus que tout, conciliant la rigueur comptable et le jugement technique nécessaire à son évolution.

À quoi ressemblera votre quotidien

 - Assumer la responsabilité et la gestion de la plateforme de grand livre auxiliaire avec une approche axée sur les résultats, en agissant comme point de contact principal pour les sujets techniques, comptables et opérationnels liés à l'enregistrement et au rapprochement des transactions

 - Diriger, faire grandir et encadrer une équipe d'ingénieur(e)s, en définissant l'orientation technique et en prônant l'exactitude dans un système où chaque écriture doit balancer

 - Veiller à ce que tous les mouvements de fonds, tant à la réservation qu'après la réservation, soient comptabilisés avec exactitude, avec une traçabilité complète de l'événement source jusqu'au rapport financier

 - Établir des relations solides de haut niveau avec les équipes Finances et Comptabilité, en traduisant les exigences comptables en conception de système et en signalant tôt les contraintes techniques

 - Repérer et saisir les occasions de réduire l'effort de rapprochement manuel, de combler les lacunes de production de rapports et d'éliminer des catégories entières d'écarts à la source

 - Suivre des indicateurs clés comme l'exactitude des rapprochements, le taux de transactions non appariées, les délais du cycle de clôture et la fiabilité du système, et diriger des revues récurrentes avec les Finances et la direction de l'ingénierie

Le ou la candidat(e) idéal(e) possède

WHO ARE WE?

ABOUT THE ROLE

We are looking for a detail-oriented and proactive Global Payroll Analyst to support and manage payroll operations across multiple countries. This individual will play an important role in ensuring accurate, timely, and compliant payroll processing while helping scale and improve our global payroll infrastructure.

The Global Payroll Analyst will partner closely with People Operations, Finance, Accounting, Benefits, and external payroll providers to manage payroll inputs, review payroll calculations, reconcile payroll results, and resolve employee and provider inquiries.

This role requires someone who is comfortable navigating the complexities of multi-state and multi-country payroll, managing competing deadlines, identifying discrepancies, and continuously looking for opportunities to streamline processes through automation and operational improvements.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

GLOBAL PAYROLL OPERATIONS

 - Support and manage end-to-end payroll processing across multiple countries, including the US, Canada, United Kingdom, Germany, France and additional international markets.

 - Coordinate payroll calendars, deadlines, employee changes, new hires, terminations, compensation changes, bonuses, commissions, and other variable compensation.

 - Collect, validate, and audit payroll inputs to ensure accuracy and completeness before each payroll submission.

 - Review payroll previews and reports, identifying discrepancies and resolving issues before payroll approval and funding.

 - Ensure payroll is processed accurately and on schedule in accordance with local requirements and company policies.

 - Partner with global payroll providers and Employer of Record (EOR) partners to resolve payroll discrepancies and address employee-specific issues.

 - Support payroll funding, payment confirmations, and post-payroll reconciliations.

PAYROLL COMPLIANCE & RECONCILIATION

 - Maintain an understanding of applicable payroll tax, statutory deductions, employer contributions, and reporting requirements across assigned countries.

 - Reconcile payroll registers against HRIS records, accounting data, and prior payroll periods.

 - Review year-to-date balances, taxable earnings, deductions, employer contributions, and statutory limits.

 - Assist with quarterly and annual payroll activities, including tax filings, year-end reporting, and audits.

 - Identify and investigate discrepancies related to payroll taxes, benefits deductions, retirement contributions, and employee earnings.

 - Maintain accurate payroll documentation and support internal and external audits.

SYSTEMS & PROCESS IMPROVEMENT

 - Help maintain and optimize our global payroll platform, HRIS, and integrations with other systems.

 - Identify opportunities to automate manual processes, improve data accuracy, and create more scalable workflows.

 - Develop and maintain payroll procedures, checklists, process documentation, and internal controls.

 - Assist with system implementations, payroll migrations, testing, and ongoing platform enhancements.

 - Partner with internal stakeholders to ensure employee data and payroll changes are accurately reflected across connected systems.

EMPLOYEE & CROSS-FUNCTIONAL SUPPORT

 - Serve as a point of contact for employee payroll inquiries, providing timely and accurate responses.

 - Partner with People Operations on onboarding, offboarding, employee changes, and payroll-related benefits administration.

 - Collaborate with Finance and Accounting on payroll reporting, journal entries, accruals, and reconciliations.

 - Work closely with Benefits and retirement plan providers to ensure accurate payroll deductions, employer contributions, and funding.

 - Build strong relationships with external payroll vendors and proactively follow up on outstanding issues.

QUALIFICATIONS

 - 3+ years of experience in payroll operations, preferably supporting multi-country or global payroll.

 - Experience processing payroll in multiple countries

 - Working knowledge of payroll taxes, statutory deductions, benefits deductions, and employer contributions.

 - Experience reviewing payroll registers, conducting reconciliations, and identifying payroll discrepancies.

 - Familiarity with payroll systems and HRIS platforms; Rippling experience is a plus.

 - Strong Google Sheets skills, including the ability to work with formulas, lookups, pivot tables, and large datasets.

 - Excellent organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple payroll calendars and competing deadlines.

 - Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with exceptional attention to detail.

 - Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with cross-functional teams.

 - Strong written and verbal communication skills.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Experience supporting payroll across the US, Canada, UK, and/or European countries.

 - Experience working with global payroll providers, EOR platforms, and managed payroll solutions.

 - Familiarity with payroll accounting, general ledger reconciliations, and payroll funding.

 - Experience with payroll system implementations, integrations, and process automation.

 - Exposure to benefits administration and retirement programs, including 401(k), RRSP, and workplace pension contributions.

 - Experience supporting payroll audits, year-end processes, and statutory reporting.

 - A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch.

 - RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme.

 - 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent.

 - Annual enrichment benefits:
   
   

HOW AND WHERE WE WORK:

 - Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly.

Who we are
 Unit8, founded in 2017, is a high-tech, dynamic Swiss leader in AI and data analytics consulting, renowned for solving complex challenges in non-digital native industries such as automotive, chemicals, financial services, manufacturing, and pharma. Our partnerships with industry leaders like Palantir, NVIDIA, and OpenAI underscore our commitment to excellence. With over 200 successful projects and a team of ~200 professionals across Switzerland, Poland, Germany, Spain and the US, we have entered the Canadian market in early 2026 and are set for further expansion.
 Our mission
 Unit8 is dedicated to driving AI adoption in non-digital industries and accelerating their digital transformation. We invest in projects that matter, including pro-bono initiatives and “engineering for good” causes.
 The opportunity
 Following our growth in Europe and our recent expansion into the US market in early 2026, Unit8 is taking its next strategic step in North America. We are looking for an entrepreneurially minded Senior Data & AI Consultant / Consulting Lead to help expandestablish our Canadian presence in Montréal.
 This is, above all, a translator role. You are the person who sits with a client's leadership, understands what actually drives their business, and turns ambiguous problems into data & AI opportunities our engineers and data scientists can build. You are the bridge between the boardroom and the build, fluent enough in both to keep them aligned from first conversation to delivered value.
 You own the delivery and transformation strategy. You propose how to bring value across the full journey, from an initial idea and analysis through to large-scale transformation, and you are a strong communicator who can sell that plan and vision to C-level executives.
 As one of our first Canadian hires, you will help shape how the practice operates, which clients we pursue, and what Unit8 becomes known for in Canada.
 What you'll do
 Your role will evolve with our clients' needs and our growth in the region. In general, you will:
 Act as the bridge between business and technology, listening for the client's real pain points and framing them as data & AI opportunities that create measurable value
 Identify and prioritise the use cases across analytics, generative, and agentic AI that genuinely move the needle, from strategy through to implementation
 Build the business case for data & AI investments, quantifying ROI, costs, and benefits so client leaders can make confident decisions
 Shape data & AI strategies and pragmatic roadmaps that align with the client's broader business strategy and priorities
 Design the target operating models that determine how data & AI teams, functions, and centres of excellence work
 Support process re-engineering: rethinking how core business processes should work once data & AI is embedded, and helping clients manage the change
 Guide clients on their journey to becoming data- and AI-driven, assessing their maturity and keeping the work anchored to business outcomes
 Own the solution like a product manager, defining what “good” looks like, keeping scope honest, and holding the team accountable to the value delivered
 Team up with our data engineers, data scientists, AI engineers, and solution architects to turn use cases into working solutions, from modern data platforms and analytics products to machine learning and AI applications
 Contribute to business development by preparing for and taking part in client conversations, workshops, and industry conferences
 Support thought leadership through white papers and industry content on data science & AI
 Who you are
 Above all, you are a consultant and a translator: someone who can hold a business conversation with senior stakeholders and a technical conversation with engineers, and carry meaning cleanly between the two. Specifically, you are:
 A trained business consultant. You built your foundation in a leading management, strategy, or business consultancy (for example a Big 4 firm, Accenture, Capgemini, or a top strategy house), with at least 2 to 3 years of genuine business consulting project experience where you learned to structure ambiguity and drive to outcomes. This is typically part of a broader career of several years.
 A natural translator. You can sit with business leaders, understand their priorities and constraints, and reframe them as data & AI opportunities, then explain the resulting solution back to the business in plain, convincing language.
 Experienced in product management. You have owned a product, solution, or roadmap and been accountable for the value it delivered, coordinating across business and technical teams to get there.
 Seasoned on strategy projects. You have worked on the strategic questions that surround data & AI: building business cases and ROI models, designing operating models, and re-engineering business processes.
 Literate and curious about data & AI. You don't need to build the models, but you understand what modern analytics, GenAI, and agentic AI make possible, and you can spot where they create real value.
 Comfortable with ambiguity. You quickly find the things that matter to a client, whether mid-project or in a business development conversation, and you exercise good judgement on where to focus.
 A relationship builder. You earn the trust of clients and teammates and build partnerships that last.
 Academically grounded. You hold a Bachelor's or Master's degree in business, engineering, IT/computer science, mathematics, natural sciences, or a related field; an MBA is welcome.
 Language 
 Unit8 operates as one international team across Switzerland, Poland, Germany, and now North America, and works with global clients; our day-to-day working language across the company and on delivery teams is therefore English, and professional fluency in English is required for this role. French is a strong asset and is valued for working with Québec-based clients and colleagues, but it is not a requirement.
 What we offer
 At Unit8, we don't just turn data into value; we empower the people who make it possible. If you are looking for a place where you can take ownership, your next chapter starts here.
 A groundbreaking opportunity and footprint. As one of our first Canadian hires, you will play a pivotal role in establishing Unit8's presence in an emerging market, shaping how the practice operates, which clients we target, and what we are known for in Canada.
 Pioneering autonomy. We offer the freedom and entrepreneurial ownership to drive our growth strategy and decide how we deliver maximum value in a new geography.
 A “builder” culture. Our consultants work shoulder-to-shoulder with engineers and data scientists who ship production systems. You'll close the loop between strategy and delivery
 Please submit your application materials exclusively in English. 
 We welcome people from all backgrounds, regardless of gender, personality, national origin, race, religion, skin color, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, marital status, disability, or veteran status.

 LLM post-training paradigms (e.g., RLHF, GRPO, reward-free methods, etc.). 
 Agentic reinforcement learning for tool-using and browsing-based LLMs trained in interactive environments. 
 Agentic evaluation and benchmarking, including design of multi-turn, verifiable reasoning tasks.

 PhD degree in Computer Science or related fields or master's degree with comparable experience.

 Solid proficiency in Python and experience with PyTorch, DeepSpeed, Megatron and other distributed training frameworks. 
 Familiarity with LLM post-training pipelines (RLHF, GRPO/PPO, SFT, LoRA, MoE, etc.) is an asset.

About the Brand & Communications Team
 The Brand & Communications team crafts and shares Affirm’s story to build trust, elevate our brand, and drive business impact. The Brand Creative team leads conceptually bold, strategically grounded work across channels—from owned content to paid media. The PR & Communications team handles internal and external messaging, ensuring our values show up in media, exec visibility, and employee storytelling. Together, we manage brand strategy, content, campaigns, media relations, and communications. We connect meaningfully with customers, partners, and the public while championing Affirm’s mission.
 About the Role 
 We want more people to understand what makes Affirm different and choose us with confidence. To make that happen, we need a rigorous understanding of our audiences and a clear, measurable view of whether our story is resonating.
 The Senior Manager, Narrative Intelligence will build the analytical intelligence function behind Affirm’s Brand & Communications strategy. You’ll connect original research, Affirm’s first-party data, brand and media measurement, behavioral signals, and external datasets to understand our audiences, identify what shapes their perceptions, and find where our story can connect more meaningfully.
 You’ll turn a complex mix of data into a clear point of view that shapes Affirm’s narrative and the work we put into the world. Then you’ll close the loop: defining how we measure narrative performance, determining what is and isn’t working, and identifying what we should do differently as a result.
 The ambition is to make intelligence an operating system for the work—not a report that arrives after it—and set a new standard for how Brand & Communications uses data to make decisions
 What You’ll Do 
 Build an evidence-based understanding of our priority audiences. Lead research and analysis into who they are, what they value, how they behave, what they believe about Affirm and the category, and what could change those beliefs. Use segmentation, surveys, behavioral data, and other analytical approaches to identify the variables that matter most.
 Develop Affirm’s narrative measurement framework. Define the metrics, methodologies, and baselines we use to evaluate narrative performance across audiences, channels, and time horizons. Partner with Analytics, User Research, Marketing, and other teams to strengthen attribution, experimentation, and our understanding of how narrative and reputation contribute to business outcomes.
 Build the team’s intelligence system. Create the tools, dashboards, analytical standards, and shared knowledge base that make audience intelligence and performance data easy to find, interpret, and apply. Help the broader team become more analytically confident over time.
 Own the narrative feedback loop. Build a continuous, data-informed picture of how Affirm’s story is landing. Diagnose what is breaking through, what is being misunderstood or ignored, where perceptions are shifting, and what the evidence suggests we should do next.
 Connect the evidence. Bring together qualitative research, surveys, brand health, media and social intelligence, search and cultural signals, campaign performance, behavioral data, and Affirm’s own customer and business data. Draw on credible external research about culture, commerce, credit, and the forces shaping how people think and behave. Find patterns, test relationships, surface contradictions, and assess the strength of the evidence.
 Turn analysis into narrative strategy. Translate findings into clear implications for Affirm’s positioning, messaging, campaigns, content, and communications planning. Partner with the Head of Story to build and evolve Affirm’s narrative based on what the data tells us.
 Design studies that answer consequential questions. Turn ambiguous business and communications questions into testable hypotheses and rigorous research. Choose the right mix of surveys, experiments, observational analysis, and qualitative inquiry to produce evidence the team can act on.
 What We Look For 
 You’re driven to understand people through data. You’re curious about the beliefs and motivations beneath human behavior and equally interested in whether the evidence supports the story being told.
 You’ve spent 12+ years in consumer analytics, audience insights, data science, measurement, strategic intelligence, quantitative research, or a related field. You’ve used analysis to shape brand, communications, marketing, product, or creative strategy.
 You’re highly fluent in quantitative research and analysis. You’re comfortable with survey design, segmentation, statistical inference, experimentation, measurement design, and large or imperfect datasets. You work directly with data, using tools such as SQL, statistical platforms, data visualization, or business intelligence tools.
 You know how to build a complete picture from different forms of evidence. You can integrate qualitative insight and quantitative analysis, account for the limits of each source, and translate concepts such as trust, relevance, reputation, and narrative resonance into thoughtful analytical frameworks.
 You turn analysis into decisions. You can take a messy body of evidence, determine which signals matter, and explain what they mean for the narrative, the work, and the choices in front of us. Your conclusions are clear, memorable, and useful to both analytical and creative audiences.
 You work well across analytical, strategic, and creative disciplines. You can collaborate credibly with data scientists and researchers, then translate the work for writers, strategists, executives, and communications leaders.
 You’d rather discover something inconvenient than confirm what everyone already believes. You test assumptions, challenge weak evidence, and follow the data—even when it complicates the current story.
 Pay Grade - N
 Equity Grade - 6
 Employees new to Affirm typically come in at the start of the pay range. Affirm focuses on providing a simple and transparent pay structure which is based on a variety of factors, including location, experience and job-related skills. Base pay is part of a total compensation package that may include monthly stipends for health, wellness and tech spending, and benefits (including 100% subsidized medical coverage, dental and vision for you and your dependents). In addition, the employees may be eligible for equity rewards offered by Affirm Holdings, Inc. (parent company).

Our certified specialists provide client-centered rehabilitation, mobility training, and daily living skills programs that help clients build confidence and thrive. We work collaboratively with ophthalmologists, optometrists, and other health care professionals, offering essential care on a referral basis in homes, workplaces, and communities across the country.  I. Scope and Summary of Primary Responsibilities 
 The Apprentice will complete a course of study and supervised practical experience to become an Orientation and Mobility Specialist eligible for Academy for Certification of Vision Rehabilitation Professionals (ACVREP) certification. The Apprenticeship is a paid-training period consisting of graduate-level University courses and a practicum under the supervision of an ACVREP certified Orientation and Mobility Specialist. Part of the coursework will require the individual to complete an in-person, simulated, and experience-based training component. 
 The scope of the O&M position provides functional expertise for people who are blind and/or partially sighted often with complex health needs to maximize skills for optimal independence.

The Applied AI Architecture team is responsible for helping developers and enterprises safely and effectively deploy OpenAI technologies in production. We act as trusted technical advisors and thought partners for customers, working side by side with their teams to identify high-value use cases, design practical architectures, and move from prototype to durable deployment.

Cybersecurity is one of the most urgent domains where AI can help. Security teams are under pressure to reason across code, logs, infrastructure, tickets, alerts, and vulnerability data faster than ever. As frontier models become more capable, organizations need deep technical guidance on how to evaluate, validate, and safely deploy AI systems in security-critical workflows.

About the Role

We are looking for a Cybersecurity Applied AI Architect to partner with customers and help them apply OpenAI models, APIs, Codex, and agentic workflows to real cybersecurity use cases. You will work with CISOs, security executives, application security leaders, SOC teams, security engineering teams, and hands-on practitioners to identify where AI can create measurable security outcomes.

This is a customer-facing technical role for someone who can move fluidly between executive strategy, practitioner-level cyber depth, and hands-on solution design. You will help customers evaluate and deploy workflows such as secure code review, vulnerability triage, threat modeling, remediation, SOC and incident response workflows, detection engineering, cloud security, GRC automation, and security validation.

You will collaborate closely with Sales, Solutions Engineering, Product, Engineering, Research, and Security to turn customer needs into safe deployment patterns, reusable field assets, and product feedback. 

In this role, you will:

 - Deeply embed with strategic customers as the technical lead for AI-enabled cybersecurity workflows, serving as a trusted partner to both security executives and technical practitioners.

 - Lead discovery across AppSec, DevSecOps, vulnerability management, SOC/IR, detection engineering, red team, cloud security, identity, and GRC automation use cases.

 - Build and deliver customer-facing demos, prototypes, workshops, proofs of concept, and reference architectures using OpenAI APIs, Codex, agents, scripts, CLIs, GitHub workflows, CI/CD systems, logs, tickets, scanners, and common security tools.

 - Scope pilots with clear success criteria, data requirements, workflow integrations, evaluation methods, security constraints, safety boundaries, and human approval points.

 - Advise customers on safe implementation patterns, including tool and function calling, structured outputs, retrieval, sandboxing, data handling, guardrails, telemetry, auditability, and approval-gated side effects.

 - Translate between CISO-level outcomes and practitioner-level implementation details so each audience understands value, risk, and practical next steps.

 - Create reusable field assets such as demo narratives, playbooks, FAQs, objection handling, qualification guides, assessment templates, and competitive positioning.

 - Validate, synthesize, and deliver high-signal feedback to Product, Engineering, Research, Security, and GTM teams based on recurring customer requirements, blockers, product gaps, and emerging cyber workflows.

 - Have 5+ years of technical consulting, solutions engineering, security architecture, cyber advisory, deployment engineering, professional services, or equivalent customer-facing technical experience.

 - Bring strong cybersecurity domain expertise across one or more areas such as application security, cloud security, identity, vulnerability management, secure SDLC, incident response, detection engineering, threat intelligence, red teaming, or security architecture.

 - Can communicate credibly with CISOs, CTOs, security executives, engineering leaders, and highly technical security practitioners.

 - Have hands-on experience building prototypes or production systems with APIs, Python or JavaScript, agents, scripts, CLIs, GitHub workflows, CI/CD systems, logs, tickets, scanners, or other common security tooling.

 We're doing $50M+ a year and scaling to $100M+ , and we want one person who owns the money so we don't run into problems as we double the business.  The mission of this role
 Own the company's money: cash, books, payments, projections and financial planning, so the CEO always knows where cash and profit stand today and where they are heading + improving terms, cash conversion cycle etc. Success is clear, accurate projections on cash flow, subscriptions and the cash conversion cycle so there are no surprises, books closed on time every month, and every payment and filing right and on time. You also own the company's credit lines, lender relationships and financial controls, so growth is always funded and every dollar is accounted for.

 We are a profitable DTC brand selling premium pet products.  Better Everyday: make the close, the cash forecast, payments and tax filing a bit faster and cleaner every month, and fix the root cause of every payment or booking error.
 Speed Is King: have the 13-week cash flow current before our Monday leadership meeting, pay bills and contractors on time, close the books on schedule, and flag a cash risk or overrun the week it shows up.
 Work Smart: automate finance work so a part-time role covers the whole function. Bank feeds and rules handle reconciliations, every tax and payment deadline has a scheduled reminder, Claude drafts the monthly finance summary from the closed books, and the cash flow forecast pulls actuals automatically.
 Overdeliver: bring the CEO the decision the numbers point to, not just the numbers, and find savings and cash-timing wins before being asked.

 Cash flow, subscriptions and the cash conversion cycle are projected clearly, so there are no surprises: projections vs actuals; cash never below the minimum balance

 Close the books on time every month with our bookkeeper and review the P&L against budget with the CEO.
 Run contractor pay, supplier and freight bills, and affiliate payouts correctly and on time.
 Project subscriptions, subscription cohorts and the cash conversion cycle, and flag anything moving against plan the week it shows up.
 Keep every sales tax and corporate tax filing right and on time with our CPA.
 Grow our credit lines and set up an asset-based lending facility so the next two quarters of POs are always funded.

About 1Password

1Password helps people use technology safely. As a Security Engineer on the Corporate Security team, you’ll build and automate practical controls across identity, devices, internal tools, Software as a Service (SaaS), and the safe adoption of artificial intelligence (AI). Reporting to the Manager, Corporate Security, you’ll help protect the company while enabling teams to work securely and move quickly.

How we’re using AI today

Our Engineering, Product, and Design teams are thoughtfully integrating AI across the full software and product development lifecycle to move faster without sacrificing quality or security. In practice, that looks like engineers using AI-assisted coding tools to accelerate reviews and catch bugs earlier, product managers synthesizing user research at scale, and designers rapidly prototyping and iterating with AI-generated mockups. We approach AI the same way we approach security: with clear principles, human accountability at every consequential decision point, and rigorous evaluation before anything ships to customers.

What we're looking for:

• Bring 3+ years of combined experience in information technology or security engineering, along with a track record of building and shipping your own solutions.

• Write strong, maintainable code in Python, Bash, Go, or a similar language, and use application programming interfaces (APIs), webhooks, configuration as code, and continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) to build reliable tooling.

• Apply hands-on knowledge across areas such as identity and access—including single sign-on (SSO), Security Assertion Markup Language/OpenID Connect (SAML/OIDC), multifactor authentication (MFA), and role-based access control (RBAC)—as well as endpoint and device security.

• Build with AI as well as use it: work comfortably in an integrated development environment (IDE), understand the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and agentic tooling, and create automation or workflows that use AI thoughtfully.

• Use tools such as structured query language (SQL) and Amazon Web Services (AWS) infrastructure to support scheduled services, reporting, and security automation.

• Balance security goals with business needs, explain technical risks and trade-offs clearly, and collaborate effectively with IT, Engineering, Product, and other security teams.

• Bring curiosity, ownership, and a growth mindset to a remote-first environment, with an interest in broadening your scope over time and giving actionable feedback when using security products internally.

What you can expect:

• Build and automate controls across identity and access, endpoint and device security, internal tools, SaaS, and AI and agentic usage.

• Take well-scoped security engineering problems from design through implementation and steady-state operation.

• Create integrations, visibility, detection, and reporting that make security work more reliable and reduce manual effort.

• Help evaluate and de-risk new AI tools and workflows, including how agents access systems and use tools, then translate those decisions into practical controls.

• Contribute to initiatives involving device trust, software authorization, security automation, and other safeguards that protect the company’s systems and data.

• Partner with IT, Engineering, Product, vulnerability management, security operations, and other teams to integrate controls into broader initiatives.

• Participate in the Corporate Security on-call rotation and security incident response, supporting the operational health of the systems and controls the team owns. Additional compensation is provided for on-call, and you’ll have opportunities to grow into larger areas of ownership over time.

USA-based roles only: The annual base salary for this role is between $123,000 USD and $172,000 USD, plus immediate participation in 1Password's benefits program (health, dental, 401k and many others), utilization of our generous paid time off, an equity grant and, where applicable, participation in our incentive programs.

 Senior Network Engineer, Network Infrastructure 
 POSITION SUMMARY 
 The Senior Network Engineer is responsible for the design, operation, and security of complex wired, wireless, and Internet-facing network infrastructures spanning multiple data centers and locations. The role requires deep expertise across enterprise routing, firewalling, VPNs, DNS, load balancing, security appliances, and large-scale wireless networks.
 KEY RESPONSIBILITIES 
 1. Design, implement, and maintain enterprise network architectures, including LAN, WAN, wireless, data center, and Internet-edge environments.
 2. Administer, configure, and troubleshoot FortiGate/Juniper SRX firewalls, including policies, NAT, routing, and VPNs.
 3. Configure, maintain, and support Cisco Layer 2 and Layer 3 switching, including VLANs, spanning tree, EtherChannel, and inter-VLAN routing.
 4. Deploy, operate, and optimize Cisco and Ruckus wireless networks, including:
 • Controller-based and cloud-managed WLAN architectures
 • SSID design, RF tuning, roaming optimization, and wireless security
 5. Deploy, operate, and support F5 Load Balancers, including LTM (DNS/GTM experience a strong plus).
 6. Design, implement, and troubleshoot dynamic routing protocols, including BGP and OSPF.
 7. Design, implement, and support IPsec and SSL VPN solutions for site-to-site and remote access connectivity.
 8. Operate and troubleshoot DNS services in an Anycast environment.
 9. Perform advanced network and wireless troubleshooting across complex, multi-vendor environments.
 10. Participate in network design reviews, infrastructure upgrades, and large-scale migrations.
 11. Ensure high availability, performance, and security of all network services.
 12. Maintain accurate network documentation, diagrams, and operational standards.
 13. Collaborate closely with security, systems, cloud, and application teams to support business and technical objectives.
 ESSENTIAL QUALIFICATIONS 
 ACADEMIC TRAINING 
 Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field.
 WORK EXPERIENCE 
 5+ years of experience in network administration or network engineering within enterprise or service-provider environments.
 Hands-on experience administering and supporting FortiGate firewalls, Juniper firewalls, Cisco Layer 2 and Layer 3 switching, Cisco and/or Ruckus wireless networks, and F5 Load Balancers.
 Experience operating enterprise-scale routing, switching, and security infrastructures in complex production environments.
 Proven experience designing, implementing, and supporting IPsec and SSL VPN solutions for site-to-site and remote access connectivity.
 Experience designing scalable, secure, and highly available wired and wireless network infrastructures.
 Demonstrated ability to troubleshoot complex, multi-vendor network issues in mission-critical environments.
 Ability to operate effectively in a fast-moving environment with competing priorities and production impact.
 Willingness to participate in an on-call rotation for after-hours support and incident response.
 SPECIFIC COMPETENCIES 
 Strong understanding and hands-on experience with routing and network protocols including OSPF/OSPFv3, BGP and MP-BGP, Spanning Tree (STP/RSTP/MST), PIM-SSM, IGMP v2/v3, HSRP, VRRP, and MPLS.
 Working knowledge of DNS architectures, including Anycast-based DNS deployments and traffic steering concepts.
 Solid understanding of network and application security principles including DDoS attack types, mitigation strategies, Web Application Firewall (WAF) placement, network segmentation, and Internet-edge security design.
 Familiarity with large-scale wireless design considerations including RF planning, roaming behavior, and high-density environments.
 Understanding of DDoS mitigation technologies and appliances, including inline and out-of-band protection.
 Knowledge of cloud networking concepts, preferably Google Cloud Platform (GCP), with exposure to other major providers such as AWS or Azure.
 Familiarity with ITSM and work management tools such as Jira and ServiceNow.
 Experience creating and maintaining network diagrams and documentation using tools such as Microsoft Visio or Lucidchart.

Le Conseil des industriels laitiers du Québec (CILQ) est à la recherche de son ou sa prochain·e président·e-directeur·rice général·e (PDG).

Vous avez une vision stratégique, le sens politique et le talent de rassembler autour d’idées porteuses? Vous aimez comprendre les enjeux complexes, influencer les décisions et transformer les idées en actions concrètes? Cette occasion pourrait vous interpeller.

QUI SOMMES-NOUS?
Le Conseil des industriels laitiers du Québec (CILQ) représente les intérêts des fabricants de produits laitiers québécois auprès des autorités gouvernementales et de toute autre instance appelée à intervenir dans le secteur laitier.

Il veille à assurer la pérennité des activités de ses membres dans le respect de l’équité. Il contribue à un développement soutenu, dynamique et structuré de l’industrie québécoise, tout en répondant aux besoins des consommateurs.

Nos actions s'appuient sur quatre valeurs fondamentales : le leadership, l’intégrité, le respect et la concertation.

VOTRE RÔLE: VOIR PLUS LOIN, RASSEMBLER ET FAIRE AVANCER L’INDUSTRIE!
Relevant du conseil d’administration, vous serez au cœur des décisions stratégiques qui influencent l’avenir du CILQ et de l’industrie laitière québécoise. Vous transformerez les enjeux en occasions d’action, les orientations en résultats et les relations en leviers d’influence.

VOTRE TERRAIN D’ACTION : INFLUENCER, MOBILISER ET PROPULSER!: Donner le cap : définir les orientations stratégiques du CILQ et conseiller le conseil d’administration sur les enjeux prioritaires de l’industrie.
 Transformer les ambitions en résultats : traduire les orientations en plans d’action concrets, mobiliser les ressources et assurer une gestion rigoureuse des activités et des budgets.
 Anticiper et défendre les intérêts des membres : suivre l’évolution des enjeux réglementaires, élaborer les positions du Conseil et piloter les stratégies d’intervention.
 Bâtir des alliances stratégiques : développer des relations d’influence avec les décideurs gouvernementaux, les partenaires et les acteurs clés du secteur, tout en recherchant des consensus durables.
 Mobiliser les talents : diriger et rallier l’équipe autour d’objectifs communs, favoriser la collaboration et soutenir la performance organisationnelle.
 Porter la voix de l’industrie : représenter le CILQ avec crédibilité et conviction auprès des médias, des partenaires, des instances gouvernementales et du public.
 Accroître le rayonnement du CILQ : renforcer les liens avec les membres, développer des partenariats porteurs et faire progresser la reconnaissance du Conseil dans son secteur.
POURQUOI CETTE OCCASION? Parce qu’il s’agit d’un rôle où la réflexion stratégique rencontre l’action, où les relations comptent autant que les décisions et où votre capacité à rassembler peut contribuer à faire progresser les intérêts de toute une industrie.  Vos avantages à la hauteur de votre ambition: : Un poste permanent à temps plein pour jouer un rôle clé dans l’industrie laitière québécoise.
 Une rémunération compétitive , qui tient compte de votre expérience.
 Une assurance collective pour prendre soin de vous.
 Un REER avec contribution de l’employeur pour contribuer à votre avenir.
 Les outils pour réussir : cellulaire et équipement informatique fournis.
 Une compensation liée aux déplacements professionnels .

Vous vous démarquez par:: Votre expérience en leadership : expérience en direction, en gestion stratégique et en collaboration avec un conseil d’administration.
 Votre vision de gestion : expérience en gestion budgétaire, en ressources humaines et en opérations.
 Votre expérience en représentation : expérience pertinente en affaires publiques, en relations gouvernementales, en lobbying ou en défense des intérêts d’une organisation ou d’un secteur.
